header.title: Modeling of Hyperrings
header.subtitle: TÜBİTAK 2209-A Project
footer.projectSummaryText:
This project aims to algorithmically model multiplicative
        hyperrings. It offers a way to experience mathematical
        structures in a computer environment.
footer.tubitakNote: This site was developed with the support of TÜBİTAK 2209-A.
footer.thanksText: We would like to thank our project advisor Dr. Elif Özel Ay and TÜBİTAK for their support.
home.heroSubtitle:
The "Concretizing Hyperrings" project, supported
          under TÜBİTAK 2209-A
home.heroText:
Our project brings the structure of hyperrings to life in a
          computer environment through a user-friendly algorithm and web
          interface. This lets students and researchers experience abstract
          mathematics firsthand, while also contributing to stronger
          encryption and secure data communication in cybersecurity.
home.exploreHyperringText1:
Hyperrings are an important area of abstract algebra. Unlike
          classical addition and multiplication, a hyperoperation produces a
          set rather than a single element as its result. This property makes
          them especially valuable in fields such as encryption, data
          security, and mathematical modeling.
home.exploreHyperringText2:
First defined in 1934 by F. Marty, hyperrings have a wide range of
          applications in both mathematical theory and applied sciences.
          Thanks to their complex operations, hyperrings can generate unique
          and strong keys, providing extra protection in cybersecurity
          systems.
home.funcAboutText:
Our function is designed to make the structure of hyperrings easy
          to understand. The set elements and rules you enter are processed
          according to the hyperring rules, and if the set satisfies the
          hyperring structure, the results are displayed on screen as a
          table. This way you can explore in practice how hyperrings, a
          theoretical structure, actually work, and better understand how
          these structures can be used in fields such as encryption,
          security, or artificial intelligence.
home.desc1: I'm a computer engineer developing homegrown technologies in artificial intelligence and cybersecurity. My goal is to turn complex theoretical concepts into functional prototypes, contributing to Turkey's technological independence.
home.desc2: I'm a computer engineering student who loves building innovative projects. I develop Java and web projects, and aim to create innovative solutions in artificial intelligence and machine learning.
home.desc3: As our project's advisor, she provides academic and technical guidance. She has supported the team in building the project's mathematical foundation and understanding the subject conceptually.
